quotes.text: Learning without thought is labour lost; thought without learning is perilous.
When you know a thing, to hold that you know it; and when you do not know a thing, to allow that you do not know it;—this is knowledge.
What you do not want done to yourself, do not do to others.
To have faults and not to reform them—this, indeed, should be pronounced having faults.
When you have faults, do not fear to abandon them.
I am not concerned that I am not known, I seek to be worthy to be known.
A man should say, I am not concerned that I have no place, I am concerned how I may fit myself for one.
